problem_2.validation_scope: competition_simulation on 2024-09..10 S-ORS layers 2/3/4, with layer 5 hidden at the scoring window's own 30% rate (validation.faithful_boundary). The scored window carries layer 5 for 70% of timestamps against this window's 99.2%, so validating against the untouched boundary reported 0.4533 for a regime the model never meets. Baseline interp 1.4687 -> 0.6079, a 58.6% improvement. Mean RMSE over four held-out windows spanning the scoring window's conditions (2025-05, 2025-06..08, 2025-11, 2024-09..10) 1.0430 -> 0.9277, winning three of the four.
problem_2.generalization_notes: Strong performance across 4/5 secondary seasonal blocks (5-block mean 1.4933 vs baseline 1.6043), with Spring 2025 slice showing higher error.
problem_2.fix_note: Layers 6/7/8 are observed for 57%/81%/40% of training timestamps but 99% of the scored window's, so the fit was dominated by a shallow-column regime the scoring window never shows - and those layers are what rebuild a missing layer-5 boundary. Training rows whose deep layers were actually measured now carry weight 4, the interior optimum of a 1/2/4/8/16 sweep. Note the earlier boundary-dropout entry was validated on two views of a single window and is weaker than stated: across the four windows it wins two and loses two (mean 1.0627 -> 1.0430). It is kept because it combines with this change better than either alone.

problem_3.validation_scope: primary_holdout 2025-03~06 plus a 3-fold rolling backtest scored over its wind-bearing cases. Wins all four model seeds on both: primary mean 0.735904 -> 0.726142, rolling mean 0.757389 -> 0.749411.
problem_3.selection_note: Wind-forcing ratios improved the primary holdout AND all three rolling folds, so unlike the subsampling step this needed no judgement call. Primary now also beats the original pre-subsampling candidate (0.737349).
problem_3.fix_note: I-ORS and S-ORS have atmospheric records only from 2025-01 while their wave records start 2024-01, so 4,749 of 10,476 training cases carry no wind at all, while 195 of the 200 scored cases have it at 97% coverage. Those cases are now weighted 0.25 instead of 1.0. Dropping them outright was measured first and lost (rolling 0.7558 -> 0.7685) because it halves the training set. The 0.25 is empirical, not a matched rate - matching the scored 97% share would need about 0.04, close to the dropping that failed.
